_desc: R4.0/R4.1 budget-integration gate — drive via tools/dm_diff_band.py --band 0 --funnel report --min-delivery full. A 2-hop alice -> relay -> bob where the relay carries a GENEROUS duty_cycle (0.1 over a 1h window -> budget 360000ms) it never approaches, so compute_budget_tier() runs on REAL sim airtime and returns HEALTHY all run: the relay CTSes normally (NO spurious BUDGET NACK) and delivery is 1/1 identical lua-vs-meshroute. This exercises the enabled-but-healthy tier path (airtime_used_ms -> pct < strained) that the FakeHal unit tests can't, and proves the R4.0 config plumb + R4.1 emit guard are INERT when budget is healthy. GATE REALITY (why no forced-CRITICAL delivery gate): (1) the BUDGET NACK only changes the PATH, not delivery success — a budget-refused RTS reroutes via the cascade-to-alt that the rts_timeout would have taken anyway, so delivery is 1/1 with OR without the NACK (delivery-band is structurally blind to it, same family as the BUSY_RX/LOOP_DUP gates declared intractable); (2) the SIM hard-enforces duty-cycle at the SAME per-node duty_cycle the firmware reads (SimController.cpp:1347), so a budget tiny enough to reach CRITICAL also blocks the node's own beacons -> peers never learn its route, and the firmware-CRITICAL band (80-100%) can't be hit robustly across engines (beacon-jitter airtime differs). => the BUDGET NACK emit + blind+requeue react are UNIT-tested (test_node_r3.cpp R4.0/R4.1, deterministic FakeHal airtime). Not runnable directly (nodes carry no engine/script).
